inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-07-31: 163.055m issued and outstanding + 9.401m unvested RSUs and unvested common stock + 0.997m unvested PSAs at target + 1.757m ESPP purchase rights (FY2026 10-K antidilutive-securities table). Excluded: 0.150m options (weighted exercise price $232.89, out of the money) and the 3.925m shares underlying the 2028 Notes (conversion price $439.52, far out of the money; the notes are carried as debt at par instead). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back ($821.923m), tying to the Note 13 expense table. Zscaler does not net-share settle (no equity-award tax line in financing activities), so there is no withholding-tax cash to add. The company's combined non-GAAP figure of $841.6m ('SBC and related payroll taxes') is NOT used as the deduction: the $19.7m difference is employer payroll tax that is already a cash cost inside operating cash flow, so it is instead left inside the EBITDA margin.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% USD: ~4.3% US 10-year risk-free + ~1.05 beta x 5.0% ERP = ~9.5% cost of equity. The only debt is a zero-coupon convertible more than covered by cash, so the capital structure is effectively all-equity and WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not a second time through the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost ($82.9m FY2026) is an operating expense inside EBITDA, so operating lease liabilities ($159.5m) are NOT in net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three scenarios (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company: tech, SaaS'). Zscaler is a US subscription-software operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no adaptations file needed (USD filer, USD quote, no NCI, operating leases). First valuation of this ticker; fresh build, no reconciliation. OWNER FCF IS NEGATIVE: reported FCF (company definition: OCF $1,129.7m - PP&E $277.3m - capitalized internal-use software $73.2m) = $779.1m; less SBC $821.9m; less interest income $136.1m (net cash $1.75bn is added to EV, so its interest is stripped) = -$178.9m. The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow of $852.4m omits capitalized software and is not used. Same series: FY2025 -$60.0m, FY2024 -$51.8m. Reported FCF grew 15% a year over FY2024-26 while owner FCF got worse, because SBC (24.3% -> 24.7% -> 24.5% of revenue) has not fallen as the business scaled. FY2026 COMPONENT ANCHORS: adj. EBITDA = non-GAAP operating income $767.1m + D&A $148.5m - employer payroll tax on SBC $19.7m = $895.9m (26.7%); D&A 4.4%; capex incl. capitalized software $350.5m (10.5%); cash tax paid $54.1m; working-capital inflow ~$170m on a $679m revenue increase (~25% capture, flattered by ~$15m non-cash lease cost). NET CASH: cash $928.4m + short-term investments $2,545.8m = $3,474.2m, less the 2028 convertible notes at $1,725.0m principal (carrying value $1,696.4m; zero coupon; mature 15 July 2028) = net cash $1,749.2m. Capped calls are given no value. BUYBACKS: none, ever. The flat share count is therefore a modelling convention the company has not paid for: basic shares rose 3.0% in FY2026 (158.3m -> 163.1m). EQUITY BRIDGE: the September 2026 restructuring (~3% of workforce, $30-33m of charges) is deducted as a one-off. NOT MODELLED: bolt-on M&A ($918m cash in FY2026, $375m in FY2024) is outside FCF; revenue growth in the paths is treated as organic from the FY2026 base. CASH TAX: the engine charges tax on post-SBC EBIT only, which is near zero in the early years, while the company already pays ~$54m a year of foreign and withholding tax on a GAAP pre-tax loss; early-year rates are set above statutory to partly reflect that, and no credit is taken for the US loss carryforwards behind the valuation allowance. Latest filing is the FY2026 10-K; Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 31 October 2026) had not been reported at the valuation date, so the price and the balance sheet are 3.5 months apart.

equity_bridge.note: Announced September 2026, $30-33m; one-off cash cost outside the margin path

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 revenue guidance ($3,908-3,938m, +16.6% to +17.5%) plus a modest allowance for the company's record of beating its initial guide
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here. Book equity grew 53% a year over three years while the company lost money in every one of them: the growth is additional paid-in capital from stock compensation ($3.87bn APIC against a $1.25bn accumulated deficit), not retained earnings. GAAP EPS is negative in every year, so EPS CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less interest income) is negative in every year of the series: FY2024 -$51.8m, FY2025 -$60.0m, FY2026 -$178.9m, so no owner-FCF CAGR can be computed. Company-defined FCF over the same years was $585.0m, $726.7m, $779.1m (+15.4% a year) while SBC went $527.7m, $661.4m, $821.9m (+24.8% a year). SBC is growing faster than cash flow: all of the reported FCF, and more, is being paid for in stock. Revenue CAGRs are FY2023-26 and FY2021-26; FY2026's 25% growth included the Red Canary and SPLX acquisitions closed in Q1 FY2026.

base.narrative: Guidance met with the usual small beat, growth fading to 5% by year 10; non-GAAP operating margin rises from 23% to about 29.5%; SBC falls 0.8pp a year to 15.8% of revenue.

bull.narrative: Security for AI and metered non-user pricing reaccelerate net new ARR; margins reach mature-security-vendor levels and SBC falls 1.1pp a year to 13%.

bear.narrative: Guidance is the ceiling, bundlers take share, and SBC stays above 20% of revenue because equity is what retains engineers when the stock is down.

scenario_narratives.base: Zscaler delivers FY2027 guidance with a one-point beat (18% against a 17% guide) and growth then fades steadily to 5% by FY2036 as the core ZIA/ZPA franchise saturates the large-enterprise base and Security for AI, Z-Flex and the Red Canary cross-sell fill part of the gap. Non-GAAP operating margin climbs from 23% to about 29.5% (EBITDA margin 35%), in line with scaled security peers. The deciding axis is stock compensation: it has sat at 24-25% of revenue for three years, and the base case assumes it finally falls, by 0.8pp a year, to 15.8%. Capex stays elevated at 10.5% of revenue in FY2027 as management has flagged, then eases toward 6%. The deferred-revenue tailwind shrinks with growth (18% capture on the revenue increase). Owner FCF turns positive in FY2028 and reaches roughly an 11% margin at maturity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Agentic-AI security and metered, non-user pricing turn out to be the second act management describes: net new ARR reaccelerates, growth holds near 20% for two years and is still 12% in year six, and platform breadth lets Zscaler hold price against Palo Alto, Cisco and Fortinet bundles. Operating leverage takes the EBITDA margin to 39% (the level of the most profitable security vendors) and a maturing workforce plus the restructuring discipline bring SBC down 1.1pp a year to 13% of revenue. This needs three separate things to go right at once: reacceleration, margin expansion, and SBC discipline the company has not yet shown.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 17% guide proves to be the start of a longer deceleration rather than a conservative opener: platform vendors bundling SSE/SASE at low or zero incremental price take share, the top-five channel partners (31% of revenue) shift volume to competitors, and the sales-leadership turnover costs a year of execution. Growth falls to single digits by year four. Margins stall near 30-31% EBITDA because go-to-market spend has to rise to defend the base, capex stays heavy, and SBC stays above 20% of revenue because equity grants are what retain engineers while the stock is down. Owner FCF stays close to zero throughout and most of the value left is the net cash.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): growth is already decelerating in the company's own guidance, SBC has not fallen in three years, and channel concentration is rising, though there is no solvency or refinancing risk with $1.75bn of net cash. Base 50%: guidance plus peer-like margin maturation is the central path. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it requires reacceleration, margin expansion and SBC discipline together, and they are largely independent.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Zscaler is valued on owner free cash flow: the cash the business generates after paying employees in full, including the quarter of revenue paid in stock, and after removing interest on a cash pile that is counted separately. On that basis the company is not yet generating cash for owners (-$179m in FY2026 against $779m of reported FCF), so the valuation rests on margin expansion and, above all, on stock compensation falling as a share of revenue. The street-basis memo value treats SBC as non-cash; the gap between the two is the size of that single assumption.
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC path: every 1pp of terminal SBC as a share of revenue moves base value by several dollars a share; it has been flat at 24-25% for three years
Terminal dependence: with owner FCF negative in year 1, nearly all of the base value is the terminal value plus net cash
Acquisitions are outside the model: $918m of cash went on M&A in FY2026; if bolt-ons are a recurring cost of sustaining growth, owner FCF is overstated
No buybacks: the flat share count is a convention; basic shares grew 3.0% in FY2026
Cash tax: the company pays foreign and withholding tax while reporting GAAP losses; the engine taxes post-SBC EBIT only
2028 convertible ($1,725m, conversion price $439.52) is treated as debt at par; above the conversion price it becomes dilution partly offset by capped calls
Balance sheet is 31 July 2026; Q1 FY2027 results were due shortly after the valuation date
